item.title: Okaloosa Island water, sewer systems shutting down ahead of Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Okaloosa County Water & Sewer will begin shutting off drinking water mains and sewage lift stations starting at noon Friday on Okaloosa Island, which is under mandatory evacuation as Hurricane Isaias approaches the area. The preemptive shutdown is necessary because storm surge from the hurricane is forecast to reach 7 to 9 feet, which officials…
item.content:encoded:
Okaloosa County Water & Sewer will begin shutting off drinking water mains and sewage lift stations starting at noon Friday on Okaloosa Island, which is under mandatory evacuation as Hurricane Isaias approaches the area.

The preemptive shutdown is necessary because storm surge from the hurricane is forecast to reach 7 to 9 feet, which officials say would cause complete failure of both systems if the infrastructure remains operational during the storm. Turning off the systems now will allow the county to restore service more quickly after the hurricane passes.

Residents and businesses still on the island are urged to prepare immediately by securing their own water supply and filling bathtubs with water for toilet flushing once the systems shut down. The county is maintaining real-time emergency updates at myokaloosa.com and through its Facebook page, facebook.com/OkaloosaCounty.

item.title: Moody, DeSantis Brief Pensacola Residents on Hurricane Isaias Preparations
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody and Governor Ron DeSantis held a briefing in Pensacola on Friday ahead of Hurricane Isaias landfall, urging residents in the storm's path to complete preparations immediately and heed local evacuation orders. "Isaias is a strong hurricane, and Floridians in the path of the storm need to take this threat seriously," Moody said…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody and Governor Ron DeSantis held a briefing in Pensacola on Friday ahead of Hurricane Isaias landfall, urging residents in the storm's path to complete preparations immediately and heed local evacuation orders.

"Isaias is a strong hurricane, and Floridians in the path of the storm need to take this threat seriously," Moody said at the briefing. "It is important everyone follows the directions of their local officials. We will weather this storm together."

Residents seeking federal assistance can contact Moody's office toll-free at 866-630-7106 or visit her Senate website for hurricane resources and preparation checklists. Those eligible for disaster aid can apply through FEMA at DisasterAssistance.gov and should have ready their home address, household names, damage descriptions, insurance information, and Social Security number.

Chris Keithley issued the declaration ahead of Hurricane Isaias, which threatens the Northwest Florida region. The highest readiness condition means mandatory evacuation for all non-essential personnel.…
item.content:encoded:
Eglin Air Force Base in Okaloosa County has declared Hurricane Condition 1 as of 9 a.m. Friday, according to WKRG News 5. Base Commander Col. Chris Keithley issued the declaration ahead of Hurricane Isaias, which threatens the Northwest Florida region.

The highest readiness condition means mandatory evacuation for all non-essential personnel. Hurricane Condition 1 is declared when a hurricane is expected to impact the installation within 24 hours or less, requiring the base to secure facilities and prepare for severe weather.

Eglin, one of the largest Air Force bases in the nation, supports critical military operations and training. The evacuation order affects thousands of military and civilian personnel who do not have essential duties during the storm. Essential personnel remaining on base are required to shelter in place in designated areas designed to withstand hurricane-force winds.

item.content:encoded:
Hurricane Isaias is expected to briefly intensify to a major Category 3 storm today before potentially weakening slightly ahead of landfall near Pensacola later tonight, according to meteorologist Ben Peine.

The storm's track continues to target the Pensacola area, though forecasters are watching for any last-minute intensity changes as it approaches the coast. Residents in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should finalize hurricane preparations immediately, as landfall is expected within hours.

This is a developing situation. Check back for updates as Isaias approaches the Florida Panhandle.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias strengthens to major hurricane, 240 miles south of Pensacola
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Hurricane Isaias has intensified into a major hurricane and is positioned about 240 miles south of Pensacola as of Friday morning, according to multiple weather reports. The storm is packing maximum sustained winds of 120 mph with a minimum central pressure of 959 millibars, measured via aircraft dropsonde. The hurricane is moving north-northeast…
item.content:encoded:
Hurricane Isaias has intensified into a major hurricane and is positioned about 240 miles south of Pensacola as of Friday morning, according to multiple weather reports. The storm is packing maximum sustained winds of 120 mph with a minimum central pressure of 959 millibars, measured via aircraft dropsonde.

The hurricane is moving north-northeast at 15 mph, putting it on a track that could bring significant impacts to the Florida Panhandle and Northwest Florida region in the coming hours. Residents and businesses in Pensacola, Escambia County, and surrounding areas should monitor National Weather Service updates and prepare for potential hurricane-force winds, heavy rainfall, and storm surge.

Emergency management officials recommend securing outdoor items, reviewing evacuation routes, and ensuring emergency supplies are stocked as the system approaches the coast.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias approaches central Gulf Coast at major hurricane strength; Pensacola area under warnings
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Hurricane Isaias is bearing down on the central Gulf Coast this morning with sustained winds near 110 mph and intensifying toward major hurricane status. The storm is positioned approximately 245 miles south of Pensacola and moving north-northeast at 15 mph, according to weather reports. Storm Surge Warnings and Hurricane Warnings remain in effect…
item.content:encoded:
Hurricane Isaias is bearing down on the central Gulf Coast this morning with sustained winds near 110 mph and intensifying toward major hurricane status. The storm is positioned approximately 245 miles south of Pensacola and moving north-northeast at 15 mph, according to weather reports.

Storm Surge Warnings and Hurricane Warnings remain in effect for the central Gulf Coast, including areas from Ocean Springs, Mississippi to the Bay/Gulf County line in Florida. The National Weather Service is urging residents in warned areas to complete all preparations immediately, as the window for final safety measures is narrowing to just a few hours.

As Isaias continues its northward track, the Pensacola area faces the threat of dangerous winds, storm surge, and heavy rainfall. Residents and businesses are advised to secure loose outdoor items, ensure emergency supplies are stocked, and finalize evacuation plans if ordered to leave.

The partnership highlights how local businesses can address a practical need for families preparing children for school, when the cost of supplies can strain household budgets.

The precautionary closure is designed to protect both public health and the shellfish resource during the storm. Big Lagoon, located in Escambia County, is…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services is temporarily closing the Big Lagoon Shellfish Harvest Area effective at sunset Thursday as Hurricane Isaias approaches the region.

The precautionary closure is designed to protect both public health and the shellfish resource during the storm. Big Lagoon, located in Escambia County, is a significant shellfish harvesting area for local watermen and commercial operators.

According to WKRG News 5, the closure will remain in effect until conditions stabilize and state officials determine it's safe to resume harvesting. Residents and commercial harvesters in the area should be aware of the temporary restriction.

item.title: Florida Health Department Proposes Relaxing School Immunization Requirements
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health held a public hearing Thursday on proposed changes to school and childcare immunization rules that would remove requirements for four vaccines while keeping others in place. Under the proposal, hepatitis B, varicella (chickenpox), Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib), and pneumococcal conjugate vaccines would no…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health held a public hearing Thursday on proposed changes to school and childcare immunization rules that would remove requirements for four vaccines while keeping others in place.

Under the proposal, hepatitis B, varicella (chickenpox), Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib), and pneumococcal conjugate vaccines would no longer be mandated for school or childcare entry in Florida. The changes would align Department rules with state statute, according to a press release from the Department. Immunizations for polio, diphtheria, measles, rubella, pertussis, mumps, and tetanus would remain required.

State Surgeon General Dr. Joseph A. Ladapo framed the proposal as expanding parental choice. "Parents know their children best, and they should be the ultimate decision-makers about their children's health," Ladapo said in a statement. The Department emphasized that removing rule requirements does not prevent parents from choosing to vaccinate their children with the affected vaccines, and that religious and medical exemptions from immunization requirements remain available under Florida law.

The public hearing is one step in Florida's rulemaking process and does not constitute final adoption of the rule. The proposal also includes updates to immunization forms, exemption procedures, and compliance reporting requirements.

item.title: Pensacola State College closes through Saturday for Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola State College will shut down all campus locations starting at 4 p.m. today and remain closed through Saturday, October 10, due to Hurricane Isaias, the college announced Thursday morning. The closure affects all classes, events, campus activities, and online courses. Emergency personnel will remain on campus during the closure. The…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola State College will shut down all campus locations starting at 4 p.m. today and remain closed through Saturday, October 10, due to Hurricane Isaias, the college announced Thursday morning.

The closure affects all classes, events, campus activities, and online courses. Emergency personnel will remain on campus during the closure. The college is taking the precaution as the hurricane approaches the region.

Library services are expected to resume Sunday, October 11, and will be available to students. The college will provide updates on its social media platforms, website at pensacolastate.edu, and through PSC Alert if conditions change.
